retrieved.title: Distance Reflects Meaning
retrieved.passage:
Distance Reflects Meaning
An embedding represents a word as a vector. Nearby vectors can capture related meanings.
“Dog” and “puppy” have related meanings, so their vectors are close together.
“Dog” and “airplane” have less in common, so their vectors are farther apart.
The dashed lines measure distance between vectors. A smaller distance represents greater similarity in this example.
[Image description] Word embedding vectors from a shared origin: dog=[4,2], puppy=[3.5,3], airplane=[0.5,3]. Dashed links show Euclidean distances from dog: 1.12 to puppy, similar meaning; 3.64 to airplane, different meaning.
Illustrative 2D embeddings. Distances calculated from the coordinates shown.
Tip
Meaning becomes something we can compare with math: “dog” is closer to “puppy” than to “airplane.”

retrieved.title: Vector Databases & Vector Search
retrieved.passage:
Vector Databases & Vector Search
A vector database stores numerical representations of your text, called embeddings.
Similar meanings sit close together.
Vector search finds chunks near the question.
The AI reads those chunks to answer.
[Image description] Whiteboard meaning map inside a vector database. Saved document chunks form travel, food, and finance clusters. The question Where can I stay lands near travel chunks, including Hotels. Vector search selects nearby chunks and returns their text. Similar meanings sit close together.

retrieved.title: How RAG Works
retrieved.passage:
How RAG Works
Find the relevant information, then give it to the AI with the question.
A question starts the search.
Illustrative animation, not a live AI call. Retrieval adds context; it does not retrain the model.

retrieved.title: The Problem: Words Aren’t Numbers
retrieved.passage:
The Problem: Words Aren’t Numbers
How do you feed words into a neural network that only understands numbers?
An embedding is a learned vector (a list of numbers) that represents a word or token. Training adjusts these numbers to help the model make predictions.
[Image description] Cat and dog embeddings compared along the same dimensions: wildness, size, and furriness. Their first two dimensions are also shown as nearby points.
Warning
Both words use the same dimensions, in the same order. These values and labels are simplified examples; real dimensions are learned and blend many concepts. Words used in similar contexts tend to have similar embeddings.

model_output.answer: An embedding represents a word as a vector, where nearby vectors capture related meanings; for example, the vectors for "dog" and "puppy" are close because they have related meanings [class4:distance-becomes-a-retrieval-primitive:1]. Vector-search-based RAG uses embeddings stored in a vector database to find document chunks that are near the question's meaning [class5:vector-databases-search-by-meaning:1]. This process adds context to the question and does not retrain the answering model [class5:building-a-tiny-rag-demo:1].
